v.rationale: All three have similar foundations: onOneServer on every task, the report scheduled in Copenhagen time, a unique queued job with a bounded lock, and batched deletes. impl-2 is the most complete and best tested. Both commands get short-expiry withoutOverlapping, so a killed run can't block the next one and a long run can't double up. Every job timing value fits inside the hour. Its tests actually run schedule:run twice in the same minute and check uniqueness against a real database queue. impl-1 has the leanest cart cleanup and excellent DST tests. However, it deliberately leaves the commands with no overlap guard, and its UniqueFor equals the one-hour interval, so after a crash the next hourly dispatch can be skipped. impl-3 has sound job timing but schedules the cart cleanup in UTC, unlike the rest of the business schedule. Its tests are weaker: one is misnamed and doesn't test what it claims, plus an expect(true) filler and awkward assertions.
